reconcile.connective: Defenders deny the premise that Abram was Terah's eldest: if he was born in Terah's 130th year, the 205-year lifespan and the age-75 departure both fit.

discrepancy.connective: The objection was pressed in detail by the Karaite polemicist Isaac of Troki, who charged that Stephen erred, since on the plain Genesis figures Abram left Haran while Terah was still alive.

skeptic.name: Isaac ben Abraham of Troki
skeptic.attribution: Isaac ben Abraham of Troki (d. 1594), Chizzuk Emunah / Faith Strengthened (1593), Part 2

excerpts.excerpt_text: Terah died two hundred and five years old, Gen 11:32; then Abram departed from Haran when seventy-five years old, Gen 12:4; therefore Abram was born, not when his father Terah was seventy, but when he was one hundred and thirty.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly works the disputed arithmetic (205 - 75 = 130) to deny that Abram was born in Terah's 70th year, which is the premise the contradiction rests on; resolves Gen 11:26 / 11:32 / 12:4 / Acts 7:4 in one stroke.

pd_work.resource: John W. Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John W. Haley
pd_work.note: Haley treats this exact Terah/Abraham chronology (Gen 11:26, 32; 12:4; Acts 7:4) directly under the harmonizing tradition.

link.title: Genesis 11:32 — Was Abraham 75 years old when he left Haran, or was he 135 years old?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment that cites Acts 7:4 and argues Abram was Terah's youngest son.
